mechanism: Caffeine inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP1A2, potentially increasing verapamil concentrations; additionally, both agents have opposing effects on heart rate and contractility (verapamil depressant vs. caffeine stimulant).
action: Counsel patients to limit caffeine intake and monitor for signs of verapamil toxicity (bradycardia, hypotension, AV block); consider alternative beverages or dose adjustment if excessive caffeine consumption occurs.
